text: BTM415 Game Theory Homework Assignment 1 Due: Thursday 26 March 2026 10:30am (in class) No late submission is allowed without a prior approval. 0 points from 10:40am. (13) Q1. Prove that any2×2game has a Nash equilibrium in mixed strategies. You don’t need to understand all the details, as some go beyond the scope of this course. The proof can be found on p121-122 of Chapter 6 in Tadelis (2013), for instance. So this question basically asks you to summarize that. (20) Q2. (Cournot Duopoly) Firms 1 and 2 produce a homogeneous product. Firmichooses to produce quantityq i ∈R + at a unit costc i, i.e., the total cost to produce quantityqi isc i(qi) =c iqi. The market clearing price isP(Q) =a−bQwhereQ=q 1 +q 2 is the aggregated quantity. (5) (a) Write down firmi’s profit maximization problem and find best response function. (5) (b) Find a Nash equilibrium. For (c-d), assumea= 150, b= 2, c1 =c 2 = 30. (5) (c) Calculate the social surplus (i.e., sum of payoffs of two firms) in equilibrium. (5) (d) Now, a social planner wants to maximize social surplus. Find the aggregated quantity and social surplus for the socially efficient outcome. (20) Q3. (Stackelberg Duopoly) Two firms in Q2 have the same characteristics, but now firm 1 chooses q1 first, and firm 2 observesq1 and choosesq 2. (15) (a) Find a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium (Do not simplify constants, e.g.,ci.) and com- pare it with Q2-(b). (5) (b) Now, fora= 150, b= 2, c1 =c 2 = 30, calculate the social surplus. (17) Q4. (Hawk-Dove) The Hawk-Dove game is used to study conflict over a valuable resource. Two players simultaneously choose either Hawk (H) or Dove (D). The value of the resource isv. If both players chooseH, they split the resource equally but each suffers an injury costk, where k > v/2. If one player choosesHand the other choosesD, the Hawk player obtains the entire resource and the Dove player gets0. If both players chooseD, they split the resource equally. (2) (a) Write the payoff matrix in terms ofvandk. (5) (b) Now letv= 10andk= 6. Find all pure-strategy Nash equilibria. (10) (c) For the same parameter values, find all (nondegenerate) mixed-strategy Nash equilibria. (30) Q5. (Sequential-move Hawk-Dove) Continued from Q4, but now consider a sequential-move Hawk- Dove game where P1 moves first. Read the strategies from left to right. (5) (a) Draw a game tree. (5) (b) What is the normal form of this game? Clearly show the payoff matrix. (5) (c) Find all pure-strategy Nash equilibria. (5) (d) Find all subgame-perfect Nash equilibria.
